title: Polymer
content: Polymer is a large molecule made by linking together repeating units of small molecules.
e: A polymer is a large molecule made by linking repeating units of small molecules. Plastics, starch, and proteins are polymers.

title: Monomer
content: Monomer is a small, reactive molecule that reacts to make long-chain molecules called polymers.
e: A monomer is a small reactive molecule that joins to make a long-chain polymer. Ethene is the monomer of polyethene.

title: Homopolymer
content: Homopolymer is a polymer that contains only one kind of monomer.
e: A homopolymer contains only one kind of monomer. Polyethene, made only from ethene, is a homopolymer.

title: Copolymer
content: Copolymer is a polymer formed from two or more different monomers.
e: A copolymer is formed from two or more different monomers. The chain therefore has more than one repeating unit type.

title: Polymerisation
content: Polymerisation is the process of linking up monomers to form a polymer.
e: Polymerisation is the process of linking monomers into a polymer. The two main kinds are addition and condensation.

title: Addition polymerisation
content: Addition polymerisation is the polymerisation in which monomers containing carbon-to-carbon double bonds react together to form long-chain molecules.
e: Addition polymerisation joins monomers that contain carbon-carbon double bonds into a long chain. Nothing small is eliminated; the double bonds simply open and link.

title: Condensation polymerisation
content: Condensation polymerisation is a polymerisation in which two molecules are joined to form a larger molecule by elimination of a small molecule, such as H2O.
e: Condensation polymerisation joins two molecules into a larger one by eliminating a small molecule such as water. Nylon and polyester form this way.

title: Biodegradable plastics
content: Biodegradable plastics are plastics that are designed to break up when exposed to the presence of microorganisms.
e: Biodegradable plastics are designed to break up when microorganisms attack them. The chain is built so bacteria or fungi can digest it.

title: Photodegradable plastics
content: Photodegradable plastics are plastics that are gradually broken down with exposure to light.
e: Photodegradable plastics slowly break down when light hits them. UV energy splits bonds in the chain.

title: Spectroscopy
content: Spectroscopy is the study of the interaction of matter and electromagnetic radiation.
e: Spectroscopy studies how matter interacts with electromagnetic radiation. You use the absorbed or emitted frequencies to identify what is there.

title: Electromagnetic radiation
content: Electromagnetic radiation is the radiant energy that displays wave properties.
e: Electromagnetic radiation is radiant energy that travels as waves. Infrared, visible light, and UV are the regions organic chemists use most.

title: Frequency
content: Frequency is the number of wave crests that pass by a given point in one second.
e: Frequency is the number of wave crests that pass a point in one second. Higher frequency means higher energy for the photon.

title: Wavelength
content: Wavelength is the distance from any point on one wave to the corresponding point on the next wave.
e: Wavelength is the distance from a point on one wave to the same point on the next wave. Infrared wavelengths are longer than visible ones.

title: Wavenumber
content: Wavenumber is the number of wave crests that pass in one centimetre.
e: Wavenumber is the number of wave crests in one centimetre. Infrared spectra are usually plotted in wavenumbers.

title: Infrared spectroscopy
content: Infrared spectroscopy is a technique for identifying compounds based on the change in vibrations of particular atoms when infrared radiation of specific frequencies is absorbed.
e: Infrared spectroscopy identifies compounds from the vibrations of particular bonds as they absorb infrared of specific frequencies. Each functional group has a characteristic absorption region.

title: Primary alcohol
content: Primary alcohol is an alcohol with a -CH3 or R-CH2- group bonded to the -OH group.
e: A primary alcohol has the OH on a carbon that is attached to only one other carbon, or it is methanol. Gentle oxidation of a primary alcohol can give an aldehyde, then a carboxylic acid.

title: Secondary alcohol
content: Secondary alcohol is an alcohol with two R- groups bonded to the carbon bearing the -OH group.
e: A secondary alcohol has two carbon groups on the carbon that holds the OH. Oxidation of a secondary alcohol gives a ketone.

title: Esterification
content: Esterification is the reaction of an alcohol with an acid to produce an ester and water.
e: Esterification is an alcohol reacting with an acid to make an ester and water. Concentrated sulphuric acid is often used as a catalyst.

title: Transesterification
content: Transesterification is the reaction of an ester with an alcohol to form a different ester.
e: Transesterification is an ester reacting with an alcohol to make a different ester. Biodiesel is made this way from fats and methanol.

title: Condensation reaction
content: Condensation reaction is the reaction in which a small molecule, such as water is eliminated when two molecules are joined.
e: A condensation reaction joins two molecules and eliminates a small molecule such as water. Esterification and nylon formation are condensation reactions.
